It reaches no store, so it answers even when the database is absent.\"\"\"\n    return {\"status\": \"ok\"}\n\"\"\"In-process test client for the application; used by acceptance and the pytest suite.\"\"\"\n\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app_server.main import create_app\n\n\ndef web_client() -> TestClient:\n    \"\"\"Return a TestClient wrapping a new application instance.\"\"\"\n    return TestClient(create_app())\ncat: fxrates_app/rates.py: No such file or directory\n----\n__init__.py\n__pycache__\nconfig.py\necb.py\nfetch.py\n----\n\"\"\"FxRates application package.\n\nApplication modules (config, ecb, fetch, rates, history, convert, commands) are added by later\nbuild blocks. The environment is read at\ncall time. Application code opens the store only through `persistence.open_database`.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\n\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nDEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH = \"data/app.db\"\nSQLITE_PREFIX = \"sqlite://\"\n\n\ndef database_path() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the database location from the environment, falling back to data/app.db.\"\"\"\n    url = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\", \"\")\n    if url.startswith(SQLITE_PREFIX):\n        url = url[len(SQLITE_PREFIX):]\n    if url:\n        return url\n    path = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\", \"\")\n    if path:\n        return path\n    return DEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH\n\n\ndef open_store() -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the store named by `database_path()` through the persistence library.\"\"\"\n    return open_database(database_path())\n----\n\"\"\"Command registry and dispatch.\n\nCommand stories register a handler under a command name at import time. `main` hands the\nremaining arguments to the handler and returns the handler's exit code.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli import usage\n\nUSAGE_ERROR = 2\n\n_handlers: dict[str, Callable[[list[str]], int]] = {}\n\n\ndef register_command(name: str, handler: Callable[[list[str]], int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Map a command name to its handler; registering a name again replaces the handler.\"\"\"\n    _handlers[name] = handler\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Validate `argv`, dispatch `argv[0]` to its registered handler, and return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    args = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)\n    try:\n        usage.validate(args, _handlers)\n    except usage.UsageError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    handler = _handlers.get(args[0])\n    if handler is None:\n        print(f\"error: command not available in this build: {args[0]}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    return handler(args[1:])\n\"\"\"Argument validation for the fxrates command line.\n\n`validate` runs before dispatch and rejects a malformed invocation with `UsageError`, so the caller\ncan exit 2 with empty stdout and one stderr line. It never opens a database or binds a socket.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Collection\n\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nPORT_FLAG = \"--port\"\nPORT_MIN = 1\nPORT_MAX = 65535\n\n# Exact positional argument counts for the commands whose stories are in the blueprint table.\n_ARITY: dict[str, int] = {\"init\": 0, \"load\": 1, \"fetch\": 0}\n_SERVE = \"serve\"\n\n\nclass UsageError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"A malformed invocation. a ``list`` filters on whichever inputs are supplied, and the inputs of a\n    ``create``, ``update``, or ``upsert`` outside ``match`` are the values written. ``row`` is the dataclass the operation returns, and\n    ``columns`` are its fields; an operation with no ``row`` returns a count. ``compare`` holds\n    ``(field, op, column)`` for each input compared other than by equality with its own column,\n    such as ``(\"start_date\", \">=\", \"date\")``, and ``order`` the ``(column, direction)`` sort keys\n    of a ``list``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    match: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    name: str = \"\"\n    compare: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = ()\n    order: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()\n\n    def keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The match fields compared by equality: what reads back the one row a write reached.\"\"\"\n        compared = {field for field, op, _ in self.compare if op != \"=\"}\n        return tuple(name for name in self.match if name not in compared)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Application code opens the store only through `persistence.open_database`.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\n\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nDEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH = \"data/app.db\"\nSQLITE_PREFIX = \"sqlite://\"\n\n\ndef database_path() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the database location from the environment, falling back to data/app.db.\"\"\"\n    url = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\", \"\")\n    if url.startswith(SQLITE_PREFIX):\n        url = url[len(SQLITE_PREFIX):]\n    if url:\n        return url\n    path = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\", \"\")\n    if path:\n        return path\n    return DEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH\n\n\ndef open_store() -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the store named by `database_path()` through the persistence library.\"\"\"\n    return open_database(database_path())\n----\n\"\"\"Command registry and dispatch.\n\nCommand stories register a handler under a command name at import time. `main` hands the\nremaining arguments to the handler and returns the handler's exit code.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli import usage\n\nUSAGE_ERROR = 2\n\n_handlers: dict[str, Callable[[list[str]], int]] = {}\n\n\ndef register_command(name: str, handler: Callable[[list[str]], int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Map a command name to its handler; registering a name again replaces the handler.\"\"\"\n    _handlers[name] = handler\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Validate `argv`, dispatch `argv[0]` to its registered handler, and return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    args = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)\n    try:\n        usage.validate(args, _handlers)\n    except usage.UsageError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    handler = _handlers.get(args[0])\n    if handler is None:\n        print(f\"error: command not available in this build: {args[0]}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    return handler(args[1:])\n\"\"\"Argument validation for the fxrates command line.\n\n`validate` runs before dispatch and rejects a malformed invocation with `UsageError`, so the caller\ncan exit 2 with empty stdout and one stderr line. It never opens a database or binds a socket.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Collection\n\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nPORT_FLAG = \"--port\"\nPORT_MIN = 1\nPORT_MAX = 65535\n\n# Exact positional argument counts for the commands whose stories are in the blueprint table.\n_ARITY: dict[str, int] = {\"init\": 0, \"load\": 1, \"fetch\": 0}\n_SERVE = \"serve\"\n\n\nclass UsageError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"A malformed invocation. The message is one line; its wording is not part of the contract.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef validate(argv: list[str], registered: Collection[str] = ()) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Raise UsageError unless `argv` names a known command with well-formed arguments.\n\n    `registered` holds the names of commands with a handler. A command outside the table above\n    and outside `registered` is a usage error; a registered command outside the table is not\n    arity-checked.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not argv:\n        raise UsageError(\"no command given; usage: fxrates <command> [arguments...]\")\n    command, rest = argv[0], list(argv[1:])\n    if command == _SERVE:\n        _validate_serve(rest)\n    elif command in _ARITY:\n        _validate_arity(command, rest)\n    elif command not in registered:\n        raise UsageError(f\"unknown command: {command}\")\n\n\ndef _validate_arity(command: str, rest: list[str]) -> None:\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return\n    expected = _ARITY[command]\n    if len(rest) != expected:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{command} takes {expected} argument(s), got {len(rest)}\")\n\n\ndef _validate_serve(rest: list[str]) -> None:\n    if not rest or rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return\n    if len(rest) != 2 or rest[0] != PORT_FLAG:\n        raise UsageError(f\"serve takes an optional {PORT_FLAG} <n>\")\n    _validate_port(rest[1])\n\n\ndef _validate_port(value: str) -> None:\n    if not re.fullmatch(r\"[0-9]+\", value) or not PORT_MIN <= int(value) <= PORT_MAX:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{PORT_FLAG} must be an integer from {PORT_MIN} to {PORT_MAX}, got {value!r}\")\n\"\"\"Command-line package: `main(argv) -> int` dispatches to handlers registered by command stories.\"\"\"\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import main, register_command\nfrom cli import init_command  # noqa: F401  registers the `init` handler at import\nfrom cli import load_command  # noqa: F401  registers the `load` handler at import\nfrom cli import fetch_command  # noqa: F401  registers the `fetch` handler at import\nfrom cli import serve_command  # noqa: F401  registers the `serve` handler at import\n\n__all__ = [\"main\", \"register_command\"]\n----\n\"\"\"Persistence access for a Drydock Target.\n\nThis file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n    \"begin_acceptance_transaction\",\n    \"end_acceptance_transaction\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n#: The comparisons a declared Match term may state; anything else is refused before SQL is built.\nCOMPARISONS = (\"=\", \"<\", \"<=\", \">\", \">=\")\nDIRECTIONS = (\"asc\", \"desc\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``name`` is the method callers use and ``verb`` is its Kind, how it runs; a name that is a\n    verb runs as that verb. ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies. ``match`` is the\n    equality predicate of a ``get``, ``update``, ``upsert``, or ``delete``, every field of it\n    required; a ``list`` filters on whichever inputs are supplied, and the inputs of a\n    ``create``, ``update``, or ``upsert`` outside ``match`` are the values written. ``row`` is the dataclass the operation returns, and\n    ``columns`` are its fields; an operation with no ``row`` returns a count. ``compare`` holds\n    ``(field, op, column)`` for each input compared other than by equality with its own column,\n    such as ``(\"start_date\", \">=\", \"date\")``, and ``order`` the ``(column, direction)`` sort keys\n    of a ``list``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    match: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    name: str = \"\"\n    compare: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = ()\n    order: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()\n\n    def keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The match fields compared by equality: what reads back the one row a write reached.\"\"\"\n        compared = {field for field, op, _ in self.compare if op != \"=\"}\n        return tuple(name for name in self.match if name not in compared)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def prepare_schema(self, sql: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Translate generated DDL for this engine.\"\"\"\n        return sql\n\n    #: Spelled by the DB-API driver, not by this class's callers.\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def connect(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def pin(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Serve one connection to every thread until ``close``. The acceptance harness's.\"\"\"\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def identity(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Name the store, so two spellings of one DSN share one acceptance transaction.\"\"\"\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def close(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def placeholder(self, index: int) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Render parameter ``index`` (0-based) in this engine's spelling.\"\"\"\n        return \"?\" if self.paramstyle == \"qmark\" else \"%s\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def quote(identifier: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Quote a declared identifier. Never called with caller-supplied text.\"\"\"\n----\n\"\"\"Generated fixtures over the configured, already provisioned application store.\"\"\"\n\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom .schema import open_database\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef committed_session():\n    \"\"\"Use normal autocommit for project tests; under the acceptance harness, its transaction.\"\"\"\n    configured = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\") or os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\") or \"data/app.db\"\n    if not configured.startswith((\"postgres://\", \"postgresql://\")):\n        if not Path(configured.split(\"://\", 1)[-1]).is_file():\n            raise RuntimeError(\"persistence store missing; rebuild the DATABASE step\")\n    database = open_database(configured)\n    try:\n        yield database\n    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef db_session():\n    \"\"\"Share this connection with the feature; always roll back, never provision schema.\n\n    Under the acceptance harness the rollback is the harness's, at the end of the criterion, so\n    a request made after this block still sees the setup.\n    \"\"\"\n    with committed_session() as database:\n        with database.rollback_session():\n            yield database","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_012ZAemopnPgyPa7S4A4ubxw","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HqcqXnxbhbmNZyW1H8aMsm","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"The `init` command: empty the rates store, print nothing, exit 0.\n\nThe schema is provisioned by the DATABASE step, so init never runs DDL or opens a driver. It\nremoves every stored rate through the declared `rates.delete_from_date` operation, passing a date\nearlier than any publication, and leaves the table in place with no rows.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\n\nEARLIEST_DATE = \"0000-01-01\"\n\n\ndef init(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Remove every stored rate and return 0. The argument list is validated before dispatch.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        db.rates.delete_from_date(from_date=EARLIEST_DATE)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"init\", init)\n----\n\"\"\"The `load` command: validate an ECB history file, store its rates, report the counts.\n\n`parse_history` checks the whole file before the first write, so a rejected file exits 3 and stores\nnothing. A file that cannot be opened or decoded exits 1 before any parsing or store access. Each rate is then written through the declared `rates.replace_rate` operation, which\nreplaces a rate already stored for the same date and currency, so loading a file twice leaves the\ndatabase unchanged.\n\nThe persistence library exposes no transaction operation, so each replace commits on its own. The\nvalidation above is what keeps a rejected file from changing anything; a store failure part way\nthrough a valid file is not rolled back.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\n\n\ndef load(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Load the file named in `rest[0]` and return the exit code. The argument list is pre-validated.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        with open(rest[0], encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as handle:\n            text = handle.read()\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {rest[0]}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    return store_and_report(rates)\n\n\ndef store_and_report(rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Store validated (date, currency, rate_text) rows and print the dates and rates counts.\n\n    Shared by `load` and `fetch`, so both commands store and report the same way.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        for date, currency, rate in rates:\n            db.rates.replace_rate(date=date, currency=currency, rate=rate)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n    dates = {date for date, _, _ in rates}\n    print(\"dates,rates\")\n    print(f\"{len(dates)},{len(rates)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"load\", load)\n----\n\"\"\"ECB history archive download: the single function in the application that opens a network connection.\n\n`download_archive` returns the bytes of the ECB history zip. The fetch command calls it through this\nmodule attribute, so a test replaces this one seam and never reaches the network.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport urllib.request\n\nECB_ARCHIVE_URL = \"https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-hist.zip\"\nTIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30.0\n\n\ndef download_archive(url: str) -> bytes:\n    \"\"\"Return the bytes served at `url`. A transport failure or timeout raises OSError.\"\"\"\n    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS) as response:\n        return response.read()\n----\n\n    return handle\n\n\ndef serve(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Serve the application until a stop signal; return 0 on a clean stop, 1 if the port is taken.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    port = _requested_port(rest)\n    if not _port_is_free(port):\n        print(f\"error: port {port} on {HOST} is already in use\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n\n    server = _ForegroundServer(uvicorn.Config(APP_PATH, host=HOST, port=port))\n    previous = {sig: signal.signal(sig, _stop_on(server)) for sig in STOP_SIGNALS}\n    try:\n        server.run()\n    finally:\n        for sig, handler in previous.items():\n            signal.signal(sig, handler)\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"serve\", serve)\n----\nCACHEDIR.TAG\nbin\nlib\nlib64\npyvenv.cfg\n[project]\nname = \"fxrates\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.11\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"fastapi>=0.162.0\",\n    \"httpx2>=2.16.0\",\n    \"uvicorn>=0.54.0\",\n]\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\n    \"pytest>=9.1.1\",\n]\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\npythonpath = [\".\"]\n----\n\"\"\"Usage validation: malformed invocations exit 2 with empty stdout and one stderr line.\n\nExercised in-process through `cli_runner` and `cli.usage.validate`; no process is spawned.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom cli import dispatcher\nfrom cli.usage import UsageError, validate\n\nMALFORMED = [\n    [],\n    [\"frobnicate\"],\n    [\"load\"],\n    [\"load\", \"a.csv\", \"b.csv\"],\n    [\"init\", \"extra\"],\n    [\"fetch\", \"extra\"],\n    [\"serve\", \"--port\", \"notaport\"],\n    [\"serve\", \"--port\"],\n    [\"serve\", \"--port\", \"0\"],\n    [\"serve\", \"--port\", \"65536\"],\n    [\"serve\", \"--port\", \"-1\"],\n    [\"serve\", \"--port\", \"1.5\"],\n    [\"serve\", \"extra\"],\n    [\"serve\", \"--port\", \"8000\", \"extra\"],\n]\n\nVALID = [\n    [\"serve\"],\n    [\"serve\", \"--port\", \"1\"],\n    [\"serve\", \"--port\", \"65535\"],\n    [\"serve\", \"--port\", \"8000\"],\n    [\"init\"],\n    [\"load\", \"x.csv\"],\n    [\"fetch\"],\n]\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef isolated_registry(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Each test registers into its own copy of the registry so commands do not leak.\"\"\"\n    monkeypatch.setattr(dispatcher, \"_handlers\", dict(dispatcher._handlers))\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"argv\", MALFORMED, ids=lambda argv: \" \".join(argv) or \"no-command\")\ndef test_malformed_invocation_exits_2_with_empty_stdout(cli_runner, argv: list[str]) -> None:\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(*argv)\n\n    assert code == 2\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"argv\", VALID, ids=lambda argv: \" \".join(argv))\ndef test_valid_invocation_passes_validation(argv: list[str]) -> None:\n    validate(argv)\n\n\n\n\"\"\"The `init` command: empties the rates store, prints nothing, exits 0.\n\nSeeds and reads back through the persistence library, and runs the command in-process through\n`cli_runner`. Stored state is read back through `db.rates` rather than inferred from output.\n\n`init` removes every row, so each test runs inside one acceptance transaction: the command and the\nread-back share one connection, and the transaction rolls back at the end. The configured store is\nnever left changed.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef test_init_removes_seeded_rates_for_a_currency(cli_runner) -> None:\n    currency = \"ZZI\"\n    date = \"1900-10-01\"\n    with db_session() as db:\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=date, currency=currency, rate=\"1.10\")\n        assert [r.date for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)] == [date]\n\n        code, _, _ = cli_runner(\"init\")\n\n        assert code == 0","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883fea79-7688-4138-99a8-ce6a7fdf07b6","uuid":"5123a2f7-dfb0-4145-b38a-2cc42876c9e6","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:21:37.987Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"The `init` command: empty the rates store, print nothing, exit 0.\n\nThe schema is provisioned by the DATABASE step, so init never runs DDL or opens a driver. The argument list is validated before dispatch.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        db.rates.delete_from_date(from_date=EARLIEST_DATE)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"init\", init)\n----\n\"\"\"The `load` command: validate an ECB history file, store its rates, report the counts.\n\n`parse_history` checks the whole file before the first write, so a rejected file exits 3 and stores\nnothing. A file that cannot be opened or decoded exits 1 before any parsing or store access. Each rate is then written through the declared `rates.replace_rate` operation, which\nreplaces a rate already stored for the same date and currency, so loading a file twice leaves the\ndatabase unchanged.\n\nThe persistence library exposes no transaction operation, so each replace commits on its own. The\nvalidation above is what keeps a rejected file from changing anything; a store failure part way\nthrough a valid file is not rolled back.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\n\n\ndef load(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Load the file named in `rest[0]` and return the exit code. The argument list is pre-validated.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        with open(rest[0], encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as handle:\n            text = handle.read()\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {rest[0]}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    return store_and_report(rates)\n\n\ndef store_and_report(rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Store validated (date, currency, rate_text) rows and print the dates and rates counts.\n\n    Shared by `load` and `fetch`, so both commands store and report the same way.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        for date, currency, rate in rates:\n            db.rates.replace_rate(date=date, currency=currency, rate=rate)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n    dates = {date for date, _, _ in rates}\n    print(\"dates,rates\")\n    print(f\"{len(dates)},{len(rates)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"load\", load)\n----\n\"\"\"ECB history archive download: the single function in the application that opens a network connection.\n\n`download_archive` returns the bytes of the ECB history zip. return 0 on a clean stop, 1 if the port is taken.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    port = _requested_port(rest)\n    if not _port_is_free(port):\n        print(f\"error: port {port} on {HOST} is already in use\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n\n    server = _ForegroundServer(uvicorn.Config(APP_PATH, host=HOST, port=port))\n    previous = {sig: signal.signal(sig, _stop_on(server)) for sig in STOP_SIGNALS}\n    try:\n        server.run()\n    finally:\n        for sig, handler in previous.items():\n            signal.signal(sig, handler)\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"serve\", serve)\n----\nCACHEDIR.TAG\nbin\nlib\nlib64\npyvenv.cfg\n[project]\nname = \"fxrates\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.11\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"fastapi>=0.162.0\",\n    \"httpx2>=2.16.0\",\n    \"uvicorn>=0.54.0\",\n]\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\n    \"pytest>=9.1.1\",\n]\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\npythonpath = [\".\"]\n----\n\"\"\"Usage validation: malformed invocations exit 2 with empty stdout and one stderr line.\n\nExercised in-process through `cli_runner` and `cli.usage.validate`; The extracted text then goes\nthrough the same `parse_history` validation and `store_and_report` path as `load`, so a rejected\nmember exits 3 and stores nothing.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport http.client\nimport io\nimport sys\nimport zipfile\nimport zlib\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.load_command import store_and_report\nfrom fxrates_app fetch_history(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Download, extract, validate, and store the ECB history; return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        archive = fetch.download_archive(fetch.ECB_ARCHIVE_URL)\n    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot download {fetch.ECB_ARCHIVE_URL}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(archive)) as zipped:\n            text = zipped.read(MEMBER_NAME).decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except (zipfile.BadZipFile, KeyError, UnicodeDecodeError, zlib.error) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {MEMBER_NAME} from the archive: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    return {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01NC3EZ4vXBtk38chdVZRKJP","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/load_command.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883fea79-7688-4138-99a8-ce6a7fdf07b6","uuid":"1338b2b2-1c99-48a8-ae26-58b35565a073","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:23:02.091Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/load_command.py","oldString":"from cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store","newString":"from cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.help import print_help\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store","originalFile":"\"\"\"The `load` command: validate an ECB history file, store its rates, report the counts.\n\n`parse_history` checks the whole file before the first write, so a rejected file exits 3 and stores\nnothing. A file that cannot be opened or decoded exits 1 before any parsing or store access. Each rate is then written through the declared `rates.replace_rate` operation, which\nreplaces a rate already stored for the same date and currency, so loading a file twice leaves the\ndatabase unchanged.\n\nThe persistence library exposes no transaction operation, so each replace commits on its own. The\nvalidation above is what keeps a rejected file from changing anything; a store failure part way\nthrough a valid file is not rolled back.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\n\n\ndef load(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Load the file named in `rest[0]` and return the exit code. The argument list is pre-validated.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        with open(rest[0], encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as handle:\n            text = handle.read()\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {rest[0]}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    return store_and_report(rates)\n\n\ndef store_and_report(rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Store validated (date, currency, rate_text) rows and print the dates and rates counts.\n\n    Shared by `load` and `fetch`, so both commands store and report the same way.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        for date, currency, rate in rates:\n            db.rates.replace_rate(date=date, currency=currency, rate=rate)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n    dates = {date for date, _, _ in rates}\n    print(\"dates,rates\")\n    print(f\"{len(dates)},{len(rates)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"load\", load)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":15,"oldLines":6,"newStart":15,"newLines":7,"lines":[" import sys"," "," from cli.dispatcher import register_command","+from cli.help import print_help"," from fxrates_app.config import open_store"," from fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history"," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01NC3EZ4vXBtk38chdVZRKJP","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017iFRVCedMU9ka6JDiXWmq7","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/load_command.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883fea79-7688-4138-99a8-ce6a7fdf07b6","uuid":"d77656ea-90a5-4a6e-9c72-643ce7d6522e","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:23:03.987Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/load_command.py","oldString":"    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0","newString":"    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return print_help(\"load\")","originalFile":"\"\"\"The `load` command: validate an ECB history file, store its rates, report the counts.\n\n`parse_history` checks the whole file before the first write, so a rejected file exits 3 and stores\nnothing. A file that cannot be opened or decoded exits 1 before any parsing or store access. Each rate is then written through the declared `rates.replace_rate` operation, which\nreplaces a rate already stored for the same date and currency, so loading a file twice leaves the\ndatabase unchanged.\n\nThe persistence library exposes no transaction operation, so each replace commits on its own. The\nvalidation above is what keeps a rejected file from changing anything; a store failure part way\nthrough a valid file is not rolled back.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.help import print_help\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\n\n\ndef load(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Load the file named in `rest[0]` and return the exit code. The argument list is pre-validated.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        with open(rest[0], encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as handle:\n            text = handle.read()\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {rest[0]}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    return store_and_report(rates)\n\n\ndef store_and_report(rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Store validated (date, currency, rate_text) rows and print the dates and rates counts.\n\n    Shared by `load` and `fetch`, so both commands store and report the same way.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        for date, currency, rate in rates:\n            db.rates.replace_rate(date=date, currency=currency, rate=rate)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n    dates = {date for date, _, _ in rates}\n    print(\"dates,rates\")\n    print(f\"{len(dates)},{len(rates)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"load\", load)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":27,"oldLines":7,"newStart":27,"newLines":7,"lines":[" def load(rest: list[str]) -> int:","     \"\"\"Load the file named in `rest[0]` and return the exit code. The argument list is pre-validated.\"\"\"","     if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:","-        return 0","+        return print_help(\"load\")","     try:","         with open(rest[0], encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as handle:","             text = handle.read()"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_017iFRVCedMU9ka6JDiXWmq7","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01C2ZLAjjvijzWxyEp8xxBcq","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/fetch_command.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883fea79-7688-4138-99a8-ce6a7fdf07b6","uuid":"30104c02-46ef-43a2-addd-542b09f0a286","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:23:06.193Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/fetch_command.py","oldString":"from cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.load_command import store_and_report","newString":"from cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.help import print_help\nfrom cli.load_command import store_and_report","originalFile":"\"\"\"The `fetch` command: download the ECB history archive, extract its CSV, and load it as `load` does.\n\nThe download is `fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive`, the single network call. It is looked up through\nits module at call time so tests replace that one seam. A failed download, bytes that are not a zip,\nor an archive without `eurofxref-hist.csv` exits 1 before any parsing. The extracted text then goes\nthrough the same `parse_history` validation and `store_and_report` path as `load`, so a rejected\nmember exits 3 and stores nothing.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport http.client\nimport io\nimport sys\nimport zipfile\nimport zlib\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.load_command import store_and_report\nfrom fxrates_app import fetch\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nMEMBER_NAME = \"eurofxref-hist.csv\"\n\n\ndef fetch_history(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Download, extract, validate, and store the ECB history; return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        archive = fetch.download_archive(fetch.ECB_ARCHIVE_URL)\n    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot download {fetch.ECB_ARCHIVE_URL}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(archive)) as zipped:\n            text = zipped.read(MEMBER_NAME).decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except (zipfile.BadZipFile, KeyError, UnicodeDecodeError, zlib.error) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {MEMBER_NAME} from the archive: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    return store_and_report(rates)\n\n\nregister_command(\"fetch\", fetch_history)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":16,"oldLines":6,"newStart":16,"newLines":7,"lines":[" import zlib"," "," from cli.dispatcher import register_command","+from cli.help import print_help"," from cli.load_command import store_and_report"," from fxrates_app import fetch"," from fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01C2ZLAjjvijzWxyEp8xxBcq","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

It is looked up through\nits module at call time so tests replace that one seam. A failed download, bytes that are not a zip,\nor an archive without `eurofxref-hist.csv` exits 1 before any parsing. The extracted text then goes\nthrough the same `parse_history` validation and `store_and_report` path as `load`, so a rejected\nmember exits 3 and stores nothing.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport http.client\nimport io\nimport sys\nimport zipfile\nimport zlib\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.help import print_help\nfrom cli.load_command import store_and_report\nfrom fxrates_app import fetch\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nMEMBER_NAME = \"eurofxref-hist.csv\"\n\n\ndef fetch_history(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Download, extract, validate, and store the ECB history; return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        archive = fetch.download_archive(fetch.ECB_ARCHIVE_URL)\n    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot download {fetch.ECB_ARCHIVE_URL}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(archive)) as zipped:\n            text = zipped.read(MEMBER_NAME).decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except (zipfile.BadZipFile, KeyError, UnicodeDecodeError, zlib.error) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {MEMBER_NAME} from the archive: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    return store_and_report(rates)\n\n\nregister_command(\"fetch\", fetch_history)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":30,"oldLines":7,"newStart":30,"newLines":7,"lines":[" def fetch_history(rest: list[str]) -> int:","     \"\"\"Download, extract, validate, and store the ECB history; {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0155VKyQEkJfufvscG8otzYi","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/serve_command.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883fea79-7688-4138-99a8-ce6a7fdf07b6","uuid":"13d4bdb9-f46f-4e48-b26b-890b6839587c","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:23:10.243Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/serve_command.py","oldString":"from cli.dispatcher import register_command\n\nHOST","newString":"from cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.help import print_help\n\nHOST","originalFile":"\"\"\"The `serve` command: run the HTTP API in the foreground on 127.0.0.1 until SIGTERM or SIGINT.\n\nThe port is validated by `cli.usage` before dispatch. Before uvicorn binds, this command probes the\nport, so a port already in use exits 1 with one stderr line and answers no requests. Uvicorn's own\nsignal capture is replaced: it re-raises a captured SIGTERM after shutdown, which would end the\nprocess by signal instead of with exit 0. Here the signal only asks the server to stop.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport contextlib\nimport signal\nimport socket\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterator\nfrom types import FrameType\n\nimport uvicorn\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\n\nHOST = \"127.0.0.1\"\nDEFAULT_PORT = 8000\nAPP_PATH = \"app_server.main:app\"\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nPORT_FLAG = \"--port\"\nSTOP_SIGNALS = (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT)\n\n\nclass _ForegroundServer(uvicorn.Server):\n    \"\"\"Uvicorn server that leaves signal handling to `serve`.\"\"\"\n\n    @contextlib.contextmanager\n    def capture_signals(self) -> Iterator[None]:\n        yield\n\n\ndef _port_is_free(port: int) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Bind the port the way uvicorn does, then release it. True when nothing else holds it.\"\"\"\n    probe = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)\n    try:\n        probe.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)\n        probe.bind((HOST, port))\n    except OSError:\n        return False\n    finally:\n        probe.close()\n    return True\n\n\ndef _requested_port(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the port named by `--port <n>`, or the default when no option is given.\"\"\"\n    return int(rest[1]) if rest else DEFAULT_PORT\n\n\ndef _stop_on(server: uvicorn.Server) -> Callable[[int, FrameType | None], None]:\n    def handle(_signum: int, _frame: FrameType | None) -> None:\n        server.should_exit = True\n\n    return handle\n\n\ndef serve(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Serve the application until a stop signal; return 0 on a clean stop, 1 if the port is taken.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    port = _requested_port(rest)\n    if not _port_is_free(port):\n        print(f\"error: port {port} on {HOST} is already in use\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n\n    server = _ForegroundServer(uvicorn.Config(APP_PATH, host=HOST, port=port))\n    previous = {sig: signal.signal(sig, _stop_on(server)) for sig in STOP_SIGNALS}\n    try:\n        server.run()\n    finally:\n        for sig, handler in previous.items():\n            signal.signal(sig, handler)\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"serve\", serve)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":18,"oldLines":6,"newStart":18,"newLines":7,"lines":[" import uvicorn"," "," from cli.dispatcher import register_command","+from cli.help import print_help"," "," HOST = \"127.0.0.1\""," DEFAULT_PORT = 8000"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_0155VKyQEkJfufvscG8otzYi","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GQHwdPnUJXfpUCYH7cr8HH","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/serve_command.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883fea79-7688-4138-99a8-ce6a7fdf07b6","uuid":"77a02035-ca32-426a-b459-bc2c3d8147ab","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:23:12.119Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/serve_command.py","oldString":"    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0","newString":"    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return print_help(\"serve\")","originalFile":"\"\"\"The `serve` command: run the HTTP API in the foreground on 127.0.0.1 until SIGTERM or SIGINT.\n\nThe port is validated by `cli.usage` before dispatch. Before uvicorn binds, this command probes the\nport, so a port already in use exits 1 with one stderr line and answers no requests. Uvicorn's own\nsignal capture is replaced: it re-raises a captured SIGTERM after shutdown, which would end the\nprocess by signal instead of with exit 0. Here the signal only asks the server to stop.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport contextlib\nimport signal\nimport socket\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterator\nfrom types import FrameType\n\nimport uvicorn\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.help import print_help\n\nHOST = \"127.0.0.1\"\nDEFAULT_PORT = 8000\nAPP_PATH = \"app_server.main:app\"\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nPORT_FLAG = \"--port\"\nSTOP_SIGNALS = (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT)\n\n\nclass _ForegroundServer(uvicorn.Server):\n    \"\"\"Uvicorn server that leaves signal handling to `serve`.\"\"\"\n\n    @contextlib.contextmanager\n    def capture_signals(self) -> Iterator[None]:\n        yield\n\n\ndef _port_is_free(port: int) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Bind the port the way uvicorn does, then release it. True when nothing else holds it.\"\"\"\n    probe = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)\n    try:\n        probe.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)\n        probe.bind((HOST, port))\n    except OSError:\n        return False\n    finally:\n        probe.close()\n    return True\n\n\ndef _requested_port(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the port named by `--port <n>`, or the default when no option is given.\"\"\"\n    return int(rest[1]) if rest else DEFAULT_PORT\n\n\ndef _stop_on(server: uvicorn.Server) -> Callable[[int, FrameType | None], None]:\n    def handle(_signum: int, _frame: FrameType | None) -> None:\n        server.should_exit = True\n\n    return handle\n\n\ndef serve(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Serve the application until a stop signal; return 0 on a clean stop, 1 if the port is taken.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    port = _requested_port(rest)\n    if not _port_is_free(port):\n        print(f\"error: port {port} on {HOST} is already in use\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n\n    server = _ForegroundServer(uvicorn.Config(APP_PATH, host=HOST, port=port))\n    previous = {sig: signal.signal(sig, _stop_on(server)) for sig in STOP_SIGNALS}\n    try:\n        server.run()\n    finally:\n        for sig, handler in previous.items():\n            signal.signal(sig, handler)\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"serve\", serve)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":65,"oldLines":7,"newStart":65,"newLines":7,"lines":[" def serve(rest: list[str]) -> int:","     \"\"\"Serve the application until a stop signal; return 0 on a clean stop, 1 if the port is taken.\"\"\"","     if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:","-        return 0","+        return print_help(\"serve\")","     port = _requested_port(rest)","     if not _port_is_free(port):","         print(f\"error: port {port} on {HOST} is already in use\", file=sys.stderr)"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01GQHwdPnUJXfpUCYH7cr8HH","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgT3tHhvjhjURBfQuR9HK","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01U97ggZeC4QXxbaxpzpMm7w","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/fxrates_app/rates.py","content":"\"\"\"Rates on a calendar day: the effective publication date and the rates published on it.\n\nThe ECB publishes on working days only, so a request for any date resolves to the latest\npublication on or before it. Rates are returned as the stored text, never converted to a float.\nReads go through `db.rates` only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom persistence import Database\n\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\n\nBASE = \"EUR\"\n\n\ndef _effective(db: Database, day: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the latest stored publication date on or before `day`, or None when none exists.\"\"\"\n    rows = db.rates.list_on_or_before(as_of=day)\n    return rows[0].date if rows else None\n\n\ndef effective_date(d: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the latest publication date on or before `d`, or None when no such date exists.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        return _effective(db, d)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n\ndef rates_on(requested: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, str]] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return (effective date, {currency: stored rate text}) for `requested`, or None.\n\n    None means no publication exists on or before `requested`. The base currency never appears in\n    the mapping.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        effective = _effective(db, requested)\n        if effective is None:\n            return None\n        rows = db.rates.list_for_date(date=effective)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return effective, {row.currency: row.rate for row in rows if row.currency != BASE}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":288,"cache_read_input_tokens":62509,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":288},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883fea79-7688-4138-99a8-ce6a7fdf07b6","uuid":"37a05c7a-119c-41f2-9ee3-c8b66cadcbc6","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:23:15.421Z","request_id":"req_011CgT3tHFQXmyb4xPCCAQNH","wire_tool_inputs":{"toolu_01U97ggZeC4QXxbaxpzpMm7w":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/fxrates_app/rates.py","content":"\"\"\"Rates on a calendar day: the effective publication date and the rates published on it.\n\nThe ECB publishes on working days only, so a request for any date resolves to the latest\npublication on or before it. Rates are returned as the stored text, never converted to a float.\nReads go through `db.rates` only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom persistence import Database\n\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\n\nBASE = \"EUR\"\n\n\ndef _effective(db: Database, day: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the latest stored publication date on or before `day`, or None when none exists.\"\"\"\n    rows = db.rates.list_on_or_before(as_of=day)\n    return rows[0].date if rows else None\n\n\ndef effective_date(d: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the latest publication date on or before `d`, or None when no such date exists.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        return _effective(db, d)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n\ndef rates_on(requested: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, str]] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return (effective date, {currency: stored rate text}) for `requested`, or None.\n\n    None means no publication exists on or before `requested`. The base currency never appears in\n    the mapping.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        effective = _effective(db, requested)\n        if effective is None:\n            return None\n        rows = db.rates.list_for_date(date=effective)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return effective, {row.currency: row.rate for row in rows if row.currency != BASE}\n"}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgT3tismL6ciRCe3RwoLV","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01WYT1pKaTCSg9s5km2LEtu2","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/fxrates_app/currencies.py","content":"\"\"\"Currency codes the store can quote: every code with at least one stored rate, ascending.\n\nThe base currency is not a stored code and is never listed. The list comes from\n`db.rates.list_currencies`, which returns one row per stored rate, so duplicates are removed here.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\nfrom fxrates_app.rates import BASE\n\n\ndef currencies() -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Return the distinct stored currency codes, ascending, without the base currency.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        rows = db.rates.list_currencies()\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return sorted({row.currency for row in rows} - {BASE})\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":496,"cache_read_input_tokens":63546,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":496},"output_tokens":16,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883fea79-7688-4138-99a8-ce6a7fdf07b6","uuid":"c3c921b1-75c7-4a1f-8e9c-9aa9e796fa5a","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:23:20.491Z","request_id":"req_011CgT3ticPS5b7t6SLXoMkt","wire_tool_inputs":{"toolu_01WYT1pKaTCSg9s5km2LEtu2":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/fxrates_app/currencies.py","content":"\"\"\"Currency codes the store can quote: every code with at least one stored rate, ascending.\n\nThe base currency is not a stored code and is never listed. The list comes from\n`db.rates.list_currencies`, which returns one row per stored rate, so duplicates are removed here.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\nfrom fxrates_app.rates import BASE\n\n\ndef currencies() -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Return the distinct stored currency codes, ascending, without the base currency.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        rows = db.rates.list_currencies()\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return sorted({row.currency for row in rows} - {BASE})\n"}}}

Where a\ntest needs exact numbers it first empties the store inside that transaction, so the expected values\nare the ones the test seeded.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the route and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef empty_store(db) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Remove every stored rate inside the acceptance transaction.\"\"\"\n    db.rates.delete_from_date(from_date=\"0000-01-01\")\n\n\ndef test_stats_reflects_the_stored_keys(web_client) -> None:\n    d1 = \"1900-09-01\"\n    d2 = \"1900-09-02\"\n    with db_session() as db:\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=d1, currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"1.1\")\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=d1, currency=\"ZZB\", rate=\"2.2\")\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=d2, currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"1.2\")\n        keys = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n        dates = sorted({k.date for k in keys})\n\n        response = web_client.get(\"/stats\")\n\n        assert    assert body[\"last\"] == dates[-1]\n        assert isinstance(body[\"dates\"], int)\n        assert isinstance(body[\"rates\"], int)\n        assert body[\"first\"] <= d1\n        assert body[\"last\"] >= d2\n\n\ndef test_stats_body_has_exactly_the_four_declared_keys(web_client) -> None:\n    body = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n\n    assert set(body) == {\"dates\", \"rates\", \"first\", \"last\"}\n\n\ndef test_stats_counts_dates_and_rates_on_an_emptied_store(web_client) -> None:\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=\"1900-09-01\", currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"1\")\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=\"1900-09-01\", currency=\"ZZB\", rate=\"2\")\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=\"1900-09-03\", currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"3\")\n\n        body = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n\n    assert body == {\"dates\": 2, \"rates\": 3, \"first\": \"1900-09-01\", \"last\": \"1900-09-03\"}\n\n\ndef test_stats_on_an_empty_store_reports_zero_and_nulls(web_client) -> None:\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n\n        response = web_client.get(\"/stats\")\n\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    assert response.json() == {\"dates\": 0, \"rates\": 0, \"first\": None, \"last\": None}\n\n\ndef test_stats_with_one_date_reports_it_as_first_and_last(web_client) -> None:\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=\"1900-09-07\", currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"1\")\n\n        body = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n\n    assert body == {\"dates\": 1, \"rates\": 1, \"first\": \"1900-09-07\", \"last\": \"1900-09-07\"}\n\n\ndef test_stats_does_not_double_count_a_replaced_rate(web_client) -> None:\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=\"1900-09-08\", currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"1\")\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=\"1900-09-08\", currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"9.99\")\n\n        body = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n\n    assert body[\"rates\"] == 1\n    assert body[\"dates\"] == 1\n\n\ndef test_stats_applied_twice_returns_the_same_body(web_client) -> None:\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n assert body[\"currencies\"] == [\"ZZA\"]\n\n\ndef test_currencies_on_an_empty_store_is_an_empty_list(web_client) -> None:\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n\n        response = Tests\nthat depend on which publications exist start from an emptied store inside that transaction.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom fxrates_app.rates import effective_date\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the route and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef empty_store(db) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Remove every stored rate inside the acceptance transaction.\"\"\"\n    db.rates.delete_from_date(from_date=\"0000-01-01\")\n\n\ndef test_exact_publication_date_returns_its_rates_as_stored_text(web_client) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-10-01\"\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=d, currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"1.50\")\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=d, currency=\"ZZB\", rate=\"2.250\")\n\n        response = web_client.get(f\"/rates/{d}\")\n\n        assert response.status_code == 200\n        body = response.json()\n        assert body == {\n            \"date\": d,\n            \"requested\": d,\n            \"base\": \"EUR\",\n            \"rates\": {\"ZZA\": \"1.50\", \"ZZB\": \"2.250\"},\n        }\n        stored = {r.currency: r.rate for r in db.rates.list_for_date(date=d)}\n        assert body[\"rates\"] == stored\n\n\ndef test_date_between_publications_resolves_to_the_earlier_one(web_client) -> None:\n    early = \"1900-10-01\"\n    late = \"1900-10-05\"\n    between = \"1900-10-03\"\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=early, currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"1.50\")\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=late, currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"1.6\")\n\n        body = web_client.get(f\"/rates/{between}\").json()\n\n    assert body[\"date\"] == early\n    assert body[\"requested\"] == between\n    assert body[\"rates\"] == {\"ZZA\": \"1.50\"}\n\n\ndef test_date_after_a_later_publication_resolves_to_it(web_client) -> None:\n    early = \"1900-10-01\"\n    late = \"1900-10-05\"\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=early, currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"1\")\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=late, currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"2\")\n\n        body = web_client.get(\"/rates/1900-10-09\").json()\n\n    assert body[\"date\"] == late\n    assert body[\"requested\"] == \"1900-10-09\"\n    assert body[\"rates\"] == {\"ZZA\": \"2\"}\n\n\ndef test_base_currency_never_appears_in_the_rates(web_client) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-10-06\"\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=d, Stored state is read back through `db.rates`.\nThe seeded test rate is in one acceptance transaction that rolls back at the end.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\nCOMMANDS = [\"init\", \"load\", \"fetch\", \"serve\"]\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"command\", COMMANDS)\ndef test_help_exits_zero_with_usage_on_stdout_and_nothing_on_stderr(cli_runner, command: str) -> None:\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(command, \"--help\")\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.strip() != \"\"\n    assert err == \"\"\n    assert command in out\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"command\", COMMANDS)\ndef test_help_prints_a_usage_line_then_a_one_line_summary(cli_runner, command: str) -> None:\n    _, out, _ = cli_runner(command, \"--help\")\n\n    lines = [line for line in out.splitlines() if line.strip()]\n    assert len(lines) == 2\n    assert lines[0].startswith(f\"usage: fxrates {command}\")\n    assert lines[1].startswith(\"summary:\")\n\n\ndef test_load_help_needs_no_file_argument(cli_runner) -> None:\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"--help\")\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.splitlines()[0] == \"usage: fxrates load <file>\"\n\n\ndef test_init_help_does_not_reset_the_store(cli_runner) -> None:\n    currency = \"ZZH\"\n    date = \"2999-09-01\"\n    text = \"6.5\"\n    with db_session() as db:\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=date, currency=currency, rate=text)\n\n        code, _, _ = cli_runner(\"init\", \"--help\")\n\n        assert code == 0\n        rows = db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency, start_date=date, end_date=date)\n        assert [r.rate for r in rows] == [text]\n\n\ndef test_fetch_help_does_not_download(cli_runner) -> None:\n    with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\") as download:\n        code, _, _ = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--help\")\n\n    assert code == 0\n    download.assert_not_called()\n\n\ndef test_help_applied_twice_prints_the_same_text(cli_runner) -> None:\n    first = cli_runner(\"serve\", \"--help\")\n    second = cli_runner(\"serve\", \"--help\")\n\n    assert first == second\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01CXYyMbLon5hS65GDKp8J3c","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Every test shares one acceptance transaction with the command, which rolls back at the\nend, so the configured store is never left changed. Test currencies use the ZZ prefix so they never\ncollide with rates already in a store.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import parse_history\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef build(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write a file the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef write(tmp_path: Path, name: str, text: str) -> str:\n    path = tmp_path / name\n    path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return str(path)\n\n\ndef stored(db, currency: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(r.date, r.rate) for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)]\n\n\ndef test_valid_file_exits_zero_and_reports_dates_and_rates(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-02\", \"1.5\", \"2\"], [\"1900-08-01\", \"0.9\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"2,3\"]\n\n\ndef test_valid_file_stores_each_rate_as_published_text(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-02\", \"0.943\", \"160.0\"]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        code, _, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n        assert code == 0\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZA\") == [(\"1900-08-02\", \"0.943\")]\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZB\") == [(\"1900-08-02\", \"160.0\")]\n\n\ndef test_all_na_date_is_not_counted_as_a_date(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(\n        tmp_path,\n        \"in.csv\",\n        build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-03\", \"1.5\", \"N/A\"], [\"1900-08-01\", \"N/A\", \"N/A\"]]),\n    )\n\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"1,1\"]\n\n\ndef test_file_of_only_na_reports_zero_and_stores_nothing(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"na.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZH\", \"ZZI\"], [[\"1900-08-05\", \"N/A\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n\n        code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n        assert code == 0\n        assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"0,0\"]\n        assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=\"1900-08-05\") == []\n        assert db.rates.list_all_keys() == before\n\n\ndef test_loading_same_file_twice_reports_the_same_counts(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-12\", \"1.5\", \"2.5\"], [\"1900-08-11\", \"1.25\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    first = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n    second = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n    assert first[0] == second[0] == 0\n    assert first[1] == second[1]\n\n\ndef test_loading_same_file_twice_leaves_stored_rates_unchanged(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, once = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n        cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n        assert db.rates.list_all_keys() == once\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZA\") == [(\"1900-08-11\", \"1.25\"), before = len(db.rates.list_all_keys())\n        cli_runner(\"load\", first)\n        cli_runner(\"load\", second)\n\n        assert len(db.rates.list_all_keys()) == before + 1\n\n\ndef test_rejected_file_exits_three_with_empty_stdout_and_one_stderr_line(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(\n        tmp_path,\n        \"bad.csv\",\n        build([\"Date\", \"ZZB\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZB\", \"\"], [[\"1900-08-31\", \"1.5\", \"\"], [\"1900-08-30\", \"1.0x\", \"\"]]),\n    )\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n\n collections.abc import Iterator\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom cli import dispatcher, serve_command\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef busy_port() -> Iterator[int]:\n    \"\"\"A port held by a listening socket for the duration of the test.\"\"\"\n    blocker = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)\n    try:\n        blocker.bind((\"127.0.0.1\", 0))\n        blocker.listen(1)\n        yield blocker.getsockname()[1]\n    finally:\n        blocker.close()\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef free_port() -> int:\n    \"\"\"A port that nothing holds at the moment the test starts.\"\"\"\n    probe = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)\n    try:\n        probe.bind((\"127.0.0.1\", 0))\n        return probe.getsockname()[1]\n    finally:\n        probe.close()\n\n\ndef test_serve_is_registered_with_the_dispatcher() -> None:\n    assert dispatcher._handlers[\"serve\"] is serve_command.serve\n\n\ndef test_busy_port_exits_1_with_empty_stdout(cli_runner, busy_port: int) -> None:\n    code, out, _err = cli_runner(\"serve\", \"--port\", str(busy_port))\n\n    assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_busy_port_writes_one_stderr_line(cli_runner, busy_port: int) -> None:\n    _code, _out, err = cli_runner(\"serve\", \"--port\", str(busy_port))\n\n    assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n\n\ndef test_busy_port_error_names_the_port(cli_runner, busy_port: int) -> None:\n    _code, _out, err = cli_runner(\"serve\", \"--port\", str(busy_port))\n\n    assert str(busy_port) in err\n\n\ndef test_port_probe_reports_a_busy_port_as_taken(busy_port: int) -> None:\n    assert serve_command._port_is_free(busy_port) is False\n\n\ndef test_port_probe_reports_a_free_port_as_available(free_port: int) -> None:\n    assert serve_command._port_is_free(free_port) is True\n\n\ndef test_port_probe_leaves_the_port_free_after_it_runs(free_port: int) -> None:\n    serve_command._port_is_free(free_port)\n\n    assert serve_command._port_is_free(free_port) is True\n\n\ndef test_default_port_is_8000() -> None:\n    assert serve_command._requested_port([]) == 8000\n\n\ndef test_explicit_port_is_read_from_the_option() Each test runs the command in-process through `cli_runner` and reads the stored state back\nthrough `db.rates`, inside one acceptance transaction that rolls back at the end.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport http.client\nimport io\nimport zipfile\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom fxrates_app import fetch\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef csv_text(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write CSV the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef zip_with(member: str, text: str) -> bytes:\n    bio = io.BytesIO()\n    with zipfile.ZipFile(bio, \"w\") as z:\n        z.writestr(member, text)\n    return bio.getvalue()\n\n\ndef stored(db, currency: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(r.date, r.rate) for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)]\n\n\ndef test_fetch_loads_archive(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-01\"\n    ra = \"1.50\"\n    rb = \"2.250\"\n    data = zip_with(\"eurofxref-hist.csv\", csv_text([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[d, ra, rb]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=data):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n        assert code == 0\n        lines = out.splitlines()\n        assert lines[0] == \"dates,rates\"\n        assert lines[1].split(\",\") == [str(1), str(2)]\n        rows = {r.currency: r.rate for r in db.rates.list_for_date(date=d)}\n        assert rows[\"ZZA\"] == ra\n        assert rows[\"ZZB\"] == rb\n\n\ndef test_fetch_download_failure(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-02\"\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", side_effect=OSError(\"network down\")):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n        assert code == 1\n        assert out == \"\"\n        assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n        assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=d) == []\n        assert len(db.rates.list_all_keys()) == len(before)\n\n\ndef test_fetch_bad_archive(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-03\"\n    wrong_member = zip_with(\"other.csv\", csv_text([\"Date\", \"ZZA\"], [[d, \"1.5\"]]))\n    not_a_zip = bytes(range(32))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = len(db.rates.list_all_keys())\n        for payload in (not_a_zip, wrong_member):\n            with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=payload):\n                code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n            assert code == 1\n            assert out == \"\"\n            assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n            assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=d) == []\n        assert len(db.rates.list_all_keys()) == before\n\n\ndef test_fetch_rejected_member(cli_runner) -> None:\n    good = \"1900-08-05\"\n    bad = \"1900-08-04\"\n    data = zip_with(\n        \"eurofxref-hist.csv\",\n        csv_text([\"Date\", \"ZZA\"], [[good, \"1.5\"], [bad, \"0\"]]),\n    )\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=data):\n            code, out, err = download.assert_called_once_with(\n        \"https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-hist.zip\"\n    )\n\n\ndef test_fetch_timeout_exits_one_and_stores_nothing(cli_runner) -> None:\n
